area: AREA 10: publish automation (youtube.json generation, measured director sign-off, step 13 publish to public Short URL)
summary: The root problem: the last mile is hand work — Claude writes youtube.json and review/director_signoff.md by hand, types youtube_upload.py/youtube_privacy.py with --watched/--approved, and drive.py ends at step 12's manifest instead of a public URL. Everything needed is already measured on disk: step_11 (scripts/episode/step_11_qc.py, judge_master/sign_master) fills review/eye_<sha8>.json with answers+evidence, qc_r2v.json carries the coverage numbers, learnings.jsonl carries every ladder terminal with its reason, and publish_lock.py + youtube_upload.refusals are the complete policy chain. The mechanism: (a) scripts/publish/metadata.py builds the title mechanically via yp.series_title + series_of(source/book.json) and spends ONE llm.structured("reasoning", ...) call (guard_spend fires inside _NativeStructuredCaller._parse, llm.py:184) for synopsis+attribution+tags grounded in plan.json lines/shots with prior episodes' youtube.json as few-shot, the AI-disclosure block appended as a code constant; (b) scripts/publish/signoff.py renders director_signoff.md purely from files it reads (eye json, qc json, T*.dq/.content.json, learnings.jsonl, attempts dirs, new review/wardrobe_<sha8>.json from a $0 local-VLM wardrobe check reusing step_11's vlm_reader pattern) and REFUSES when any source is missing or stale, so the sign-off can never claim an unmeasured check; (c) a new scripts/episode/step_13_publish.py calls youtube_upload.main (its existing send= seam) with --watched=<sha8> — the gate text decision: --watched keeps its exact meaning and chain (eye_review.refusals lines 196-208 untouched); the judge-filled eye_<sha8>.json IS the watch under 2026-10-01-no-human-input-at-publish — then flips public via youtube_privacy (public_gates unchanged), polls https://www.youtube.com/shorts/<id> for 200, records everything in uploads.jsonl, and prints the public Short URL as drive.py's last deliverable line. The only new human artifact is a one-time owner-written library/<book>/publish/standing.json that step 13 translates into --approved=publish; absent it, the step parks with an Escalation, and RENDER_HOLD still stops everything.

gates.where: scripts/publish/metadata.py::check(meta, plan, book_json, priors) — called by generate() after each LLM round and re-checked by step_13_publish.run() before upload; youtube_upload.metadata() (youtube_upload.py:77-86) stays the final consumer and still refuses a missing file or missing "synthetic" key
gates.rule: HARD. (1) title == yp.series_title(display_title, N, total, plan['title'], series=series) exactly (series_of from scripts/publish/youtube_retitle.py:89 — refuses when source/book.json lacks series/display_title/episodes; never hardcode); (2) description contains AI_DISCLOSURE constant verbatim and attribution_line contains the book title and 'public domain'; (3) every capitalized proper noun in synopsis_paragraphs appears in plan.json (title/setups/shots/lines) or a prior episode's description (grounding — no invented people/places); (4) yp.spec() walls (title 100, description 5000, tags 500 chars) pass; (5) youtube.json carries "_for": {"plan_sha8": plan_verdict.plan_sha8(plan_path)} and is regenerated when it goes stale. Cure: one re-ask round cap 2 via llm.re_ask quoting the exact failed checks; terminal = mechanical fallback description assembled from the plan's narration lines in order (marked "_fallback": true) so the pipeline never blocks on prose

gates.where: scripts/publish/signoff.py::write(home, sha8) — its output is validated by the UNCHANGED studio/publish_lock.py::signoff_stops (lines 85-95: sha8 named, SECTIONS ('Watched','Take strips','Coverage','Flags') each >= MIN_SECTION chars)
gates.rule: HARD. write() raises SystemExit listing every missing/stale input before writing a byte: review/eye_<sha8>.json must exist for THIS sha8 and clear eye_review.refusals(); qc report must carry qc['sha8'] == yp.sha8(master); every take must have both T*.dq.json and T*.content.json (judged.unjudged_takes(folder, kinds=('dq','content')) empty — same call as youtube_upload.failed_takes line 111); learnings.jsonl must exist. Every sentence in the generated file is a template slot filled from a parsed number or verdict string — the module has no free-text parameters, so an unmeasured claim is unrepresentable. Signed line names the generator and its inputs: 'Signed: judge:signoff@v1 from eye_<sha8>.json, qc_r2v.json, NN dq/content reports, learnings.jsonl, wardrobe_<sha8>.json'

gates.where: studio/wardrobe_drift.py::judge(reads, rows) — run by signoff.py over the contact frames already cached at review/work/<sha8>/f*.png (eye_review.grab output), written to review/wardrobe_<sha8>.json, surfaced in the sign-off's Flags section and in eye ledger flags
gates.rule: ADVISORY (hard=False): a drift row {at, character, expected: [tokens from refs.json row], seen: [VLM tokens], missing: [...]} is a recorded flag, never a stop — ep18 shipped with the narrator's boater flagged and the per-chapter-sheet decision is still the owner's. The VLM (comfy.cached_text, WORKFLOW image_qwen3vl_caption, same pattern as step_11_qc.vlm_reader lines 87-101) is asked only to LIST headwear/outer-garment/colour in a closed vocabulary; the comparison against refs.json row text happens in code (panel_content rule: 'the model is never asked whether the picture is right'). $0, local GPU

HARD. library/<book>/publish/standing.json must exist with {"kind": "publish", "decision": "2026-10-01-no-human-input-at-publish", "by": <owner>, "at": <date>}; the step then appends --approved=publish to both upload and privacy argv (approval.require/approved_for in studio/approval.py:46-72 untouched, RENDER_HOLD still stops first). Absent or malformed: raise studio.escalate.Escalation('G-STANDING', 'publish/standing.json', 'write the standing publish approval once per book') — the unit parks, nothing uploads. This is the one new owner artifact; written once, it is the owner's standing hand, which the 2026-10-01 ruling already is in prose

gates.where: existing scripts/publish/youtube_privacy.py::public_gates (line 55) and scripts/publish/youtube_upload.py::refusals/eye_stops/lock_stops — ZERO changes to the policy chain
gates.rule: HARD, unchanged: qc sha8 match, no unjudged take, file_refusals (Short length + 1:1), publish_lock.stops (open terminals auto-cleared only via gate_policy state:auto, speaker_check, the now-generated sign-off), eye_review.refusals for --watched. step_13 passes --watched=<yp.sha8(master)> and the existing chain verifies the judge-filled rubric; the gate text printed by step 13: '--watched=<sha8>: the master eye's measured rubric review/eye_<sha8>.json is the watch (judge:master_eye, decision 2026-10-01-no-human-input-at-publish)'

ADVISORY TERMINAL: GET https://www.youtube.com/shorts/<id> (follow redirects; pass when the final URL still contains '/shorts/' and status==200) every 30 s, cap 600 s. Outcome appended to uploads.jsonl as {"event": "shorts_poll", "video_id", "status", "final_url", "at"}; a non-Short answer (redirect to /watch) or timeout writes a learnings.jsonl row gate=G-SHORTS action=flag terminal=true note=<status> and prints it — the video is already public, so this records truth rather than stopping. drive.py's log then ends with the URL line either way

cures.how: scripts/publish/metadata.py::generate(book, number): title/privacy/synthetic are MECHANICAL (yp.series_title + series_of(source/book.json); privacy 'private' — the flip makes it public; synthetic: true constant for this pipeline); _synthetic_note is MECHANICAL: library/<book>/publish/pipeline_note.txt (book's model stack, seeded once from the prior episode's note) + f'Cut {sha8}: QC passed, {takes}/{takes} takes, {n} judge-signed terminals auto-cleared.'; ONE llm.structured(tier='reasoning', prompt, ShortMetadata, retries=3) call for synopsis_paragraphs/attribution_line/tags — class ShortMetadata(BaseModel): synopsis_paragraphs: list[str]; attribution_line: str; tags: list[str]. Few-shot = the 2 newest prior episodes/ep*/youtube.json under the SAME library/<book>/ (code tree stays book-neutral); first episode of a book falls back to library/<book>/publish/footer.txt or parks. guard_spend fires automatically inside _NativeStructuredCaller._parse (llm.py:184) because step 13 runs in-process under episode.py's llm.spend_context — metadata MUST be imported and called in-process by step_13, never via ctx.run_script (a subprocess has no _SPEND context and would bypass the $3 wall). Retry: llm.structured's built-in 3 schema re-asks; plus cap-2 grounding re-ask via llm.re_ask(prompt, exc) when G-META checks 2/3 fail; terminal → mechanical fallback description from the plan's narration lines, '_fallback': true
cures.prompt_template:
You are writing the YouTube description and tags for one episode of a serialized public-domain book adaptation. The ONLY facts you may use are in this brief; name no character, place or event that is not named here.

BOOK: {display_title} by {author}; series label "{series}"; this is episode {number} of {total}.
CHAPTER: "{chapter_title}"

THE EPISODE'S LINES, in order (every word actually heard):
{lines_block}

THE EPISODE'S SHOTS (frame + motion, abridged to one line each):
{shots_block}

PRIOR EPISODES OF THIS SERIES, for voice and format — match their tone, tense, paragraph rhythm and tag style; do not copy their events:
{few_shot_block}

Return exactly:
- synopsis_paragraphs: 2 to 4 short present-tense paragraphs telling what happens in THIS episode using only the lines and shots above; the last paragraph may land on the episode's closing beat and may quote one short line of dialogue from the lines block. No URLs, no hashtags, no channel name, no AI-disclosure text (it is appended separately).
- attribution_line: one sentence naming the chapter exactly as "{chapter_title}", the book, the author, its year if a prior episode's attribution names one, and that it is in the public domain — same shape as the priors.
- tags: 18 to 24 lowercase search tags, each 30 characters or fewer, no '#': start from the series' recurring tags {series_tags} (the intersection of the priors' tag lists, computed by the caller) and add this episode's own people, places and things from the brief.
cures.est_cost_usd: ~$0.005 actual on gpt-5.6-luna (≈12k tokens in @ $0.20/M, ≈1.5k out @ $1.20/M); guard_spend's conservative estimate ≈ $0.016 (EXPECTED_OUTPUT_TOKENS=13000); worst case with 2 grounding re-asks ≈ $0.05 — noise under the $3 ceiling

risks: The /shorts/ 200 poll is a heuristic: YouTube serves 200 behind consent/region interstitials and may lazily classify Shorts for minutes; mitigated by the 600 s cap, final-URL-contains-/shorts/ check, and recording the honest answer as an advisory flag instead of failing a published episode

An unverified API project forces private on videos.update too: the flip can return 'private' after asking 'public'; youtube_privacy already records what YouTube returned, and step 13 must then end with the youtu.be URL plus a printed NOT-PUBLIC flag rather than claiming a public Short (never claim an unmeasured state)

standing.json is a new owner artifact — until the owner writes it once per book, every run parks at G-STANDING; this is deliberate (approval stays the owner's hand) but must be surfaced in the drive Telegram message or ep19 stalls silently

Grounding check (proper nouns ⊂ plan + priors) can false-refuse on legitimate inflections ('Martians' vs 'Martian'); stem matching reduces it, and the mechanical fallback guarantees forward progress at the cost of a plainer description

metadata called via subprocess would silently bypass guard_spend (fresh process, empty _SPEND) — the in-process rule is enforced only by test_step_13_runs_metadata_in_process; a future refactor to ctx.run_script would reopen the hole

The wardrobe check inherits every VLM-list failure mode (hat vocabulary mismatch, face-to-character attribution via shot_at on a drifted cut); it is advisory for exactly that reason, and its rows feed the owner's open per-chapter-sheet decision rather than a gate

youtube_upload.py title wall: yp.spec refuses '<'/'>' and 100 chars — yp.series_title already elides, but a pathologically long display_title+series could still trip G-META; the gate catches it before any network call
